overview: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the centre of South America. Its capital and largest city is Asunción. Paraguay became independent from Spain in 1811. It is one of the few countries where most people speak an Indigenous language, Guarani, and both Guarani and Spanish are official languages.

geography.text: The Paraguay River divides the country in two. The east is greener and more fertile and is home to most people, while the west, called the Chaco, is a hot, dry region of scrubland. The Itaipu Dam on the Paraná river, built together with Brazil, is one of the largest hydroelectric plants in the world.

history.text: Guarani peoples lived in Paraguay when the Spanish arrived, and Jesuit missions later organised many of them into settlements. Paraguay became independent in 1811. The War of the Triple Alliance from 1864 to 1870 against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay killed a huge share of its population. General Alfredo Stroessner ruled as dictator from 1954 to 1989.

events.title: War of the Triple Alliance
events.text: A catastrophic war against three neighbours begins.

events.title: Chaco War
events.text: Paraguay wins a war with Bolivia over the Chaco.

government.text: Paraguay is a presidential republic. The President is elected for a single five-year term. Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies. Paraguay was ruled by the dictator Alfredo Stroessner from 1954 to 1989.

economy.text: Paraguay is a big exporter of soybeans and beef. The Itaipú dam, shared with Brazil, is one of the largest hydroelectric plants in the world and makes Paraguay a major exporter of electricity.

culture.text: Paraguay is one of the few countries in the Americas where an Indigenous language is spoken by most people: almost everyone speaks Guaraní, and most also speak Spanish. Ñandutí, delicate spider-web lace, and tereré, a cold herbal drink, are national symbols.

items.title: Guaraní
items.text: Spoken by most Paraguayans, an official language alongside Spanish.

items.title: Tereré
items.text: Cold yerba mate tea, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Jesuit missions
items.text: Ruined mission towns from the 1600s and 1700s, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Paraguay won the Copa América in 1953 and 1979 and reached the World Cup quarter-finals in 2010. The headquarters of CONMEBOL, South American football's governing body, is near Asunción.

items.text: Reached the men's World Cup quarter-finals.

items.title: José Luis Chilavert
items.text: A goalkeeper who scored more than 60 goals, many from free kicks.

didYouKnow: Paraguay is one of only two landlocked countries in South America.
Paraguay's flag has different designs on the front and back.

keyPeople.name: José Luis Chilavert
keyPeople.text: Scored more than 60 goals in his career.
